models.title: Additivity of financial amounts valued at one date
models.summary: Cash-flow amounts and stream values can be added when they are indexed at a common valuation date.

relationship.original_equation: Amounts of money indexed at the same point in time are additive.
relationship.locator: Learning Module 1, The Cash Flow Additivity Principle, printed p38 (PDF p48), Exhibit 15; unequal-cash-flow PV printed p25/PDF35 Exhibit 10
relationship.translation_notes: Introduced family values maps the source prose to sum over same-date amounts. Currency terms add to currency. The same record supports sums of present values or future values; these are not minted as separate models. Individual cash-flow discounting is the covered discrete lump-sum relationship. Independent source contains a typo in Eq9.22; corroboration uses the explicit common-date addition prose and Table9.6, not that typo.

variables.source_symbol: amounts indexed at the same point in time
variables.definition: Values of individual cash flows or streams already transported to a common date
variables.context: Same currency, price basis and valuation date; no double counting

variables.definition: Combined signed financial value at that common date
variables.context: Same currency, price basis and valuation date as values

assumptions: Source assumption: amounts share one date before addition.
Source assumption: values share currency and nominal/real basis and represent distinct, nonoverlapping cash-flow claims.
limitations: Raw differently dated cash flows must first be discounted or accumulated; this record does not perform that transformation.
Family bounded to 256 terms per evaluation; family inverses are unavailable.

models.title: Rule of 72 approximate annual doubling time
models.summary: A footnote gives the Rule of 72 as an ad hoc approximation for the number of annual periods needed to double an investment.

relationship.original_equation: Approximate doubling periods = 72 / annual interest rate stated in percent
relationship.locator: Learning Module 1, Solving for the Number of Periods, printed p32 (PDF p42), footnote 9 (Rule of 72)
relationship.translation_notes: r is already a decimal unit-1 rate. The normalized heuristic coefficient .72 is attributed in constants, not an additional percent conversion applied by the engine. Financial-year count is dimensionless. Comparison at r=.08 gives heuristic9 versus exact9.00647; approximation uncertainty is not measurement uncertainty.

variables.definition: Annual-compounding interest rate as a decimal
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

variables.definition: Heuristic financial years to double principal under annual compounding

constants.meaning: Rule-of-72 approximation coefficient normalized for decimal rate input
constants.locator: Printed p32/PDF42 footnote9; Pearson p208/PDF11 gives 72/(100r)

assumptions: Source assumption: annual discrete compounding at a constant positive rate.
Application profile: 5%-12% rate range follows inspected Pearson corroboration, narrower than the unqualified CFA heuristic.
limitations: Approximate, with no rigorous source error bound. Exact time is log(2)/log(1+r), already an inverse of the covered discrete lump-sum model.
No prediction of future achieved returns is asserted.

models.title: Relative frequency of a category or bin
models.summary: Relative frequency normalizes a category or bin count by the number of observations in its reference dataset.

relationship.original_equation: Relative frequency = absolute frequency / total number of observations
relationship.locator: Learning Module 2, Summarizing Data Using Frequency Distributions, printed pp71-72 (PDF pp81-82), definition and Exhibit 8
relationship.translation_notes: Source prose translated directly to f/n. Integer count units cancel to dimensionless fraction; no multiplication by100 is performed. Cumulative relative frequency is this same definition applied to a prefix-bin count, not a renamed model.

Source assumption: f and n are counts; integrality is a semantic input contract, not expressible by the available guard operators.
limitations: Relative frequency is an empirical fraction, not automatically a model probability.
Row or column conditional frequencies use the corresponding marginal count as n; distinct reference sets must be explicit.
